provenance.title: Launch HN: Freestyle – Sandboxes for Coding Agents

facts.statement: The cofounders of Freestyle are Ben and Jacob.
Freestyle describes its product as "Sandboxes for Coding Agents."
Freestyle states that the current generation of AI coding agents can utilize the full power of a computer sandbox, enabled by advances beyond minimal tools and basic serverless apps.
Freestyle moved to its own bare metal racks because cloud providers' bare metal nodes were too costly and did not meet performance requirements for moving VMs across nodes.
Freestyle provides sandboxes that are interchangeable with EC2 virtual machines from an agent's perspective, running full Debian with systemd init instead of runc.
Freestyle sandboxes support full Linux capabilities including hardware virtualization, eBPF, FUSE, multiple users, and systemd services.
Freestyle was publicly launching on Hacker News in April 2026.
Freestyle provides powerful Linux VMs and Git repos for code agents did not write, enabling real VMs with sandbox environments and Git-backed filesystems.
facts.value: Powerful Linux VMs and Git repos for code you didn't write

facts.statement: Freestyle VMs provision in under 600 milliseconds from API request to ready machine.
Freestyle VMs can live fork, cloning a running VM without pausing it, providing full copies in milliseconds.
Freestyle VMs support pause and resume, hibernating VMs and resuming exactly where left off, with customers paying nothing while VMs are paused.
Freestyle Git provides every agent a branchable filesystem with commits, diffs, rollback, and review capabilities.
Freestyle supports bidirectional sync between Freestyle Git repositories and GitHub repositories.
Freestyle's VMs are full Linux VMs with real root access, supporting nested virtualization including running VMs inside VMs and Docker.
Freestyle VMs provide features like sealed Linux users, systemd services, groups, multi-user isolation, and the full Linux networking stack with real root access.
Freestyle offers a free-to-start plan with no credit card required to get started.
Freestyle's pricing plans include Free (up to 10 concurrent VMs), Hobby ($50/month, up to 40 concurrent VMs), Pro ($500/month, up to 400 concurrent VMs), and Enterprise with custom pricing.
Freestyle charges $0.04032 per hour of vCPU beyond included amounts, $0.0129 per hour of GiB memory beyond included amounts, and $0.000086 per hour of GiB storage beyond included amounts.
Freestyle pricing features include limits per plan such as maximum concurrent VMs, saved VMs, snapshots, total vCPUs, total memory, total disk, and max vCPUs, memory, and disk per VM.
There is no information about funding or capital raised in the provided records.
The 'freestyle-sh/Adorable' GitHub repository had 800 stars as of 2026-08-23.
The 'freestyle-sh/Adorable' GitHub repository has 4 human contributors and 1 bot, with the most active contributor being JacobZwang with 147 commits.
Freestyle is trusted by companies including vly.ai, Rork, and Vibeflow, as shown on its website.
The freestlye-sh GitHub account is an organization account.
Freestyle maintains an open-source project called 'Adorable' under the MIT license that is an AI app builder using Freestyle cloud VMs with git-backed persistence.
The Adorable repository's four human contributors include named individuals JacobZwang, theswerd, willothy, and bhaktatejas922.
